title: Opinionated retry presets, idempotency key format, and polyglot streaming ergonomics with examples
creator: Marco Li
description: Define and ship a small set of opinionated retry/backoff presets for Python/TypeScript/Go SDKs, a canonical idempotency key format that works across HTTP and streaming calls, and clear streaming ergonomics (resume, dedup, and semantics) with code examples and migration guidance. This ticket codifies defaults, trade-offs, and cross-language examples so client libraries behave consistently for most application workloads.
acceptance_criteria: Three named retry presets (interactive, steady, throughput) implemented in python/js/go SDKs with documented default parameters
Canonical idempotency key schema defined and libraries expose helper to generate/validate keys
Retryable error taxonomy documented (4xx vs 5xx, transient gRPC codes, transport errors) and mapped in each SDK
Streaming contract: resume token shape, deduplication window, at-most-once guidance and sample code per language
Integration tests in each SDK that assert retry/backoff behavior for simulated transient failures
Migration guide and 'breaking change' notes for users who currently implement ad-hoc keys or nonstandard backoffs
technical_notes: Preset names chosen: interactive (low latency, minimal retries), steady (balanced latency/cost), throughput (aggressive batching & retries)

Default parameters (baseline): interactive: initial=50ms, max=200ms, multiplier=1.5, max_attempts=2; steady: initial=100ms, max=1s, multiplier=2.0, max_attempts=4; throughput: initial=250ms, max=5s, multiplier=2.5, max_attempts=6
Use jittered exponential backoff with decorrelated jitter (per AWS article) to avoid synchronization spikes
Idempotency key schema: redwood:{sdk_short}:{env}:{timestamp_ns}:{random_hex8} where sdk_short is py/ts/go and env is 'hosted'|'dedicated'|'private'
Server-side expectations: keys are opaque to server but must be stable for retry window; default deduplication window 5 minutes for synchronous requests and 30s for streaming append/progress events
Streaming resume token: base64({session_id}|{sequence_offset}|{last_idempotency_key_fragment}) — libs expose helpers to parse/generate

For streaming, recommend server provide last-acked-offset and a resume_ttl; client should treat resumes as best-effort and avoid strong exactly-once semantics unless application-level de-dup is implemented

Mapping retryable errors: retry on network/timeouts (ECONNRESET, ETIMEDOUT), HTTP 408, 429 (rate-limit with Retry-After honored), 5xx (500,502,503,504), gRPC UNAVAILABLE/RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED; do NOT retry 400/401/403/404 unless explicitly marked retryable by server
Streaming-specific transient codes include CANCELLED (if network blip) and UNAVAILABLE; apply a more conservative backoff preset for streams to avoid excessive reconnections
Backwards compatibility: keep current SDK default behavior when not opting into named presets; presets opt-in via client config and exported constants
decisions: Provide opt-in presets rather than global changing defaults to avoid breaking existing customers
Use a single canonical idempotency key format to maximize cross-language reproducibility but allow override by callers
Favor clear examples and helper writers in each SDK instead of heavy runtime magic that infers idempotency from payloads
Expose a small public API: RetryPolicy(preset='steady'|'interactive'|'throughput' or custom params), IdempotencyKey.generate(sdk='py'|'ts'|'go', env='hosted') and StreamResume.parse/format
tradeoffs: Aggressive retrying (throughput preset) reduces client-visible errors but increases load and cost on servers — mitigated by server-side rate limiting and circuit breakers
Rigid idempotency format simplifies cross-lang tooling but may leak environment info (env) — minimized by keeping fields non-sensitive and allowing opt-out
Providing resume helpers for streams simplifies client code but could encourage misuse where exact-once semantics are required; docs must emphasize best-effort resume and app-level dedup
Honoring Retry-After for 429/503 is user-friendly but complicates tests and needs careful parsing of both seconds and HTTP-date formats
rollout_plan: Week 1: Finalize presets and idempotency schema; write design doc and RFC; gather sign-off from infra and security
Week 2: Implement helpers in Python SDK + unit tests and basic integration harness; open PR and request API & runtime review
Week 3: Implement TypeScript + Go SDK helpers; reuse shared test scenarios in language-agnostic harness; add CI smoke tests
Week 4: Docs + migration guide published; console/observability teams validate telemetry for retry counts and dedup windows
Week 5: Beta release; invite a handful of customers to opt-in and collect metrics; iterate on parameters
Week 8: GA release, add presets to SDK changelogs and sample starter project templates
